title: Fictional Alternate-History Demographic Scenario — 2026
note: Fictional alternate-history scenario for 2026; not a census or a real-world religious population projection. Heritage sites inform editorial settlement priors, never the observed religion of present-day residents.
capacityFormula: For each tehsil: district settlement base / mapped-tehsil count × town-centrality multiplier × mean(agriculture, industry, corridor connectivity, water) × terrain accessibility. Scores are positive integer millionths. District and division capacities sum constituent tehsils. Hierarchical largest-remainder allocation uses integer arithmetic; no land-area population allocation is used.
religionMethod: Tehsil heritage/settlement priors are balanced to locked province religion totals and integer tehsil populations by iterative proportional fitting and deterministic minimum-cost integer rounding. All higher-level communities aggregate the same tehsil records.
urbanMethod: A bounded urban/rural matrix fits tehsil settlement-type odds to exactly 40% provincial urbanization. Urban religious counts apportion each tehsil urban total within its religious inventory; rural counts are the complements.
lahoreCityDevelopment: In this fictional 2026 scenario, Lahore is the principal Sikh metropolis: a 45-lakh city with universities, technology, healthcare, modern infrastructure, commerce and heritage tourism. Its Islamic, Sikh and Hindu architectural heritage remains represented. These are worldbuilding assumptions, not measured development statistics.
ratingNote: Capacity, infrastructure, agriculture, water and accessibility scores are explicit fictional development assumptions based on the existing named centres and the user brief. They are not measured road lengths, economic indices, land-cover yields or migration forecasts. Geometry is used only for area/density and point containment.
